(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; NBC News's own reporting language)
International Brent crude oil rose almost 5% to more than $95 per barrel for the first time in almost six weeks. U.S. crude oil (WTI) rose more than 4% to more than $88 per barrel.
The price of oil surged nearly 5% as U.S. officials talked down the chance of new peace talks after an 11th straight night of strikes on Iran and with major disruption now facing two of the world's key supply routes.
Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen said they would seek to impose a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia; the "Bab el-Mandeb risk picture is deteriorating," the strait that is the gateway to the Red Sea. Like the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab el-Mandeb is a critical transit route for global oil supplies.
The national average price per gallon rose 4 cents from Tuesday to $4.06 per gallon, according to motor club AAA data tracked by NBC News.
